name: @fjellrute/mobile
//: Phases 2 and 3 of Fjellrute-Mobile-Build-Plan.docx: the Expo app. It shares packages/core with apps/web — geometry, the saved-routes client, the i18n store, the Kartverket and NVE layer descriptors — so there is exactly one definition of each and no drift between phone and laptop.
//versions: The four pinned versions below are not guesses: they were read off a working SDK 57 scaffold produced by create-expo-app on 2026-08-25 (spikes/webview-3d/app). Everything Expo manages on top of them — expo-router, expo-secure-store, expo-location, the MapLibre native module — is installed by ./setup.sh through `expo install`, which resolves the version each package must have for THIS SDK. That indirection is deliberate. Hand-written version ranges for native modules are how you get a build that compiles and then crashes on the device, and this project has already lost an evening to an Expo version that was inferred rather than read.

scripts.//web: There is deliberately no `web` script. `expo start --web` cannot run this app: MapLibre React Native has no web renderer, and expo-secure-store has no web implementation, so there is nowhere for the session to live. A script that is guaranteed to fail is worse than no script — it reads as a supported path.
scripts.//typecheck: Not wired into the root `pnpm build`. That runs `tsc -b` over the project references in the root tsconfig.json, where packages/core is compiled with `types: []` to keep it platform-free; adding this app there would put React Native's types into the same solution and the boundary harness would lose its meaning. Run it from here instead.

dependencies.//react-native-gesture-handler: These next three are here despite nothing in app/ or src/ importing them. expo-router and @expo/ui declare them as PEER dependencies, and pnpm installs missing peers automatically — resolving each to the newest version satisfying the peer's own range, which is not the version Expo pinned for this SDK. Undeclared, they were invisible to `expo install --fix`, which audits package.json and therefore reported everything up to date while the tree held worklets 0.12.1 against Expo's 0.10.1. Native autolinking does not care that no JavaScript imports them: expo-modules-core compiles C++ against react-native-worklets' headers, and 0.12.1 had dropped the WorkletRuntime::executeSync that it calls, so the Android build failed in the C++ compiler. Declaring them at the versions in expo/bundledNativeModules.json is what makes the resolution explicit rather than emergent; the root package.json also overrides them so a second copy cannot exist for autolinking to find. Change these only to match bundledNativeModules.json — scripts/verify-mobile-app.mjs compares the two.
